meta.purpose: Recall-conditioned decomposition of the shipped-engine LanceDB tear. Splits every episode into 'both indexes returned the same per-query recall' (recall_A_vs_exact == recall_B_vs_exact) and 'different per-query recall'. Only the equal-recall subset is a confound-free 'same quality, different answer' rate; the unequal subset tears mechanically because recall = |top10 n exact10| / 10.

field_semantics.tear_all: fraction of episodes with set_equal == False (= the paper's any-difference tear).
field_semantics.n_eq: episodes with recall_A_vs_exact == recall_B_vs_exact (per-query recall equal).
field_semantics.tear_eq: tear_all restricted to the n_eq subset; the CONFOUND-FREE tear.
field_semantics.tear_ne: tear_all restricted to the n_ne subset; mechanically 1.0 (see mechanical_check).

meta.recall_quantum_note: k=10 so every recall value is a multiple of 0.1; equality is exact and unambiguous.

cell_naming.matched2_lance_cells: match2_{hnsw|ivfpq}_s{seed}_<level>; 60 cells = 2 families x 3 seeds x 10 levels.

levels.default: genA default search -> optimize() -> genB default search (unequal effort).
levels.samegen_control_A/B: same generation searched twice, no maintenance (must be 0).
levels.R09/R095/R099: recall-matched pair (fine knob search, window +/-0.01) at target R=0.90/0.95/0.99.
levels.F_default/F_R09/F_R095/F_R099: floor_lance: same-order rebuild (same data, same insertion order, index rebuilt) at default or at the given target R.

mechanical_check.claim: per-query recall differs => top-10 sets differ (tear == 1.0); i.e. tear_ne == 1.0 for every cell.

pin_alignment.claim: Both sides of the pinned/unpinned comparison carry per-episode recall, so the same conditioning applies to the pin experiment.

caveats.matched_gap_not_always_le_0p004: The 'matched' rows are aligned by minimizing the pair gap under a window around the target, but the 3-seed worst seed can exceed 0.004 (e.g. ivfpq R0.90: gaps 0.002/0.017/0.003, so 1/3 seeds miss the target). The floor rows routinely miss it too (hnsw F_R0.95 gaps up to 0.0205). Report per-cell gaps, not just the mean.
caveats.lancedb_matched_vs_floor_share_genB: LanceDB matched compares genA (fresh create_index) vs genB (post-optimize rebuild); the floor compares genB vs genR2 (create_index(replace=True)). The two comparisons SHARE the genB build, so their tear estimates are correlated (the floor is NOT an independent baseline). The builds available in the data are only {genA, genB, genR2}; no pair is independent of both comparisons, so a fully independent floor would require a fresh rebuild (e.g. genR3), i.e. an engine re-run.
caveats.lancedb_has_no_permutation: Unlike pgvector (matched = id-order vs permuted-order), the LanceDB rewrite (optimize()) does NOT reorder rows: genA and genB are both same-data, same-order builds. So the LanceDB 'matched' comparison is itself a same-order rebuild comparison, which is the structural reason its tear does not separate from the floor.
caveats.pgvector_floor_is_independent: pgvector's floor (id-order CREATE INDEX vs id-order REINDEX) shares no build with its matched pair (id-order vs permuted) -- the two estimators are constructed differently across engines; the matched/floor RATIO is comparable but the absolute construction is not.
